headline: Theodore Roosevelt National Park Entry and Backcountry Access
reservation: Park entry requires a standard pass payable at stations in Medora or the North Unit. Backcountry camping requires a specific permit obtained in person at the South Unit or North Unit visitor centers; systems for site reservations and trail access evolve, so check the official park portal for current seasonal availability.

days.title: Medora and the South Unit Loops

stops.name: Painted Canyon Overlook
stops.detail: Witness the expansive geological strata of the Badlands from a high-altitude vantage point before entering the valley floor.

stops.name: Scenic Loop Drive
stops.detail: Navigate the 36-mile paved circuit to observe prairie dog towns and potential bison sightings among the multi-colored buttes.

days.driving: Allow 2–3 hours for the loop; conditions vary with wildlife movement.
days.note: Early starts are recommended to avoid mid-day summer heat on exposed trails.

days.title: North Unit Wilderness Landscapes

stops.name: River Bend Overlook
stops.detail: View the dramatic meanders of the Little Missouri River against the backdrop of jagged sedimentary cliffs.

stops.name: Oxbow Overlook
stops.detail: The terminus of the North Unit road offers a panoramic view of the river's historic course and deeply eroded canyons.

days.driving: Allow 1.5 hours between units; gravel spurs may be impassable when wet.
days.note: The North Unit is more remote and generally quieter than the South Unit.

days.title: Historic Ranching and River Bottoms

stops.name: Elkhorn Ranch Site
stops.detail: Reach the secluded location of Roosevelt's 'home ranch' to experience the solitude of the river valley.

stops.name: Wind Canyon Trail
stops.detail: A short walk above the river provides one of the best perspectives on the wind-sculpted formations.

days.driving: Allow 2 hours for the ranch road; high-clearance vehicles are recommended for unpaved sections.
days.note: River crossings and dirt roads are subject to weather-related closures.

intel.title: South Unit Trailheads
intel.text: Parking at popular trailheads like Wind Canyon can reach capacity during autumn weekends. Overflow parking is restricted to designated areas to protect fragile prairie ecosystems.

intel.title: Remote Unit Connectivity
intel.text: Cellular service is intermittent in the North Unit and largely non-existent at Elkhorn Ranch. Carry physical maps for navigation outside of the main paved loops.

intel.title: Gateway Supply Points
intel.text: Medora and Watford City serve as the primary hubs for fuel and provisions. Ensure tanks are full before entering the North Unit as no services exist inside the park boundary.

intel.title: Wildlife Congestion
intel.text: Bison frequent the roadways in the South Unit, often causing significant travel delays. Maintain a safe distance and allow extra time for these natural traffic stoppages.

intel.title: Seasonal Road Closures
intel.text: Segments of the Scenic Loop Drive may close due to winter snow or spring washouts. Check the current road status at the Medora Visitor Center upon arrival.

plan.arrival: Collect rental vehicles in Bismarck or Dickinson; stock up on water and supplies in Dickinson before the final drive to Medora.
plan.vehicle: Standard cars are sufficient for paved loops, but high-clearance vehicles are advised for the Elkhorn Ranch road.
plan.goldenHour: Wind Canyon Overlook, where the light emphasizes the river meanders, though shadows lengthen early in the deep draws.
